message.content:
I'm investigating a vague bug report from the user of a Next.js/Tailwind POS app at G:\PROJECT1\KasirKu (KasirKu). Their exact words (Indonesian, somewhat garbled): "saya ga tau ya kenapa bisa lemot, kurang responsif jadi loading nya lama. dan untuk menulis baik di email pasword, jumlah kembalian semuanya abu-abu jadi kadang ga keliatan sama sekali" — roughly: "I don't know why it's slow/laggy, loading takes a while. And for typing in email/password, the change amount [kembalian] is all grey so sometimes it's not visible at all."

I need you to investigate TWO separate possible UI bugs (don't investigate performance/slowness — that's a separate, vaguer concern I'll ask about separately):

1. **Login/signup page input text color**: Read src/app/login/page.tsx and src/app/signup/page.tsx (and src/components/auth-shell.tsx if relevant). Look at the email and password `<input>` elements' Tailwind classes. Is there any class that would make TYPED TEXT inside these inputs render in a low-contrast grey color (e.g. text-zinc-400, text-gray-300, placeholder-only styling accidentally applied to real input text, missing an explicit text color so it inherits something too light)? Report the exact className strings for the email and password inputs in both files.

2. **POS "Kembalian" (change due) display**: Search the codebase (grep for "Kembalian" and "kembalian") to find every place a change-due amount is displayed on the POS/checkout screen (likely under src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/ or similar checkout/payment components). For EACH match, report the file path, line number, and the exact Tailwind className used to render the kembalian VALUE (the number itself, not the label) — I specifically need to know if it uses a grey/muted text class (text-zinc-400, text-gray-400, text-zinc-300, etc.) that could render as invisible or hard-to-read against its background, especially if that background is also light/white or grey.

For both investigations: quote the exact code snippet (a few lines around each match) so I can see the full className and surrounding context (parent background color if in the same snippet). Don't propose fixes — I'll design those myself. Report factually, concisely, under 500 words total.

content.text:
Investigation complete. Findings below. ## 1. Login/signup input text color **src/app/login/page.tsx** — email input (line 59) and password input (line 79): ``` className="w-full rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 px-3.5 py-2.5 text-sm transition-shadow focus:border-brand-600 focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-brand-100" ``` **src/app/signup/page.tsx** — email (line 97), password (line 112), confirm-password (line 130), all identical: ``` className="w-full rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 px-3.5 py-2.5 text-sm transition-shadow focus:border-brand-600 focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-brand-100" ``` None of these six `` elements set an explicit `text-*` color class — no `text-zinc-400`/grey class is present. `src/components/auth-shell.tsx` (line 73) puts the form card on `bg-white/95`. I did not find any `input { color: ... }` or `@layer base` rule in `src/app/globals.css` overriding input text color (no matches). So typed text should inherit whatever the global default text color is (not an explicit grey utility) — I could not confirm a grey-text root cause here; the classNames themselves contain no grey color class. ## 2. Kembalian display Four matches render the change-due **value**, all via `formatRupiah(...)`: - **src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx:613** ```jsx

Kembalian: {formatRupiah(change)}

``` Label and value share one `

` styled `text-zinc-500` (grey), on whatever the surrounding panel background is (not shown in this snippet). - **src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/ticket-pos-screen.tsx:1284-1286** ```jsx

Kembalian: {formatRupiah(change)}

``` Same pattern, `text-zinc-500`. - **src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/ticket-reports/[transactionId]/page.tsx:133-137** ```jsx
Kembalian {formatRupiah(Number(transaction.change))}
``` Parent div sets `text-zinc-600`; inherited by both label and value ``s (value span has no override). - **src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/transactions/[transactionId]/page.tsx:141-146** ```jsx
Kembalian {formatRupiah(Number(p.change))}
``` Same `text-zinc-600` pattern. - **Receipt pages** (`ticket-reports/[transactionId]/receipt/page.tsx:133-137` and `transactions/[transactionId]/receipt/page.tsx:150-154`) render Kembalian with no explicit text color class on the wrapping `
` (just `flex justify-between`), so no grey class applies there. All four "grey" instances use `text-zinc-500` or `text-zinc-600` (not the very light `text-zinc-300/400`), but none override with a darker/higher-contrast class for the value itself — the value always inherits the same grey as its label.
